quest.title: Unofficial Chronicle of the Desert Pavilion
quest.description: There appears to be a survivor who's escaped punishment at the Desert Pavilion...

chapter.num: A Long Day in the Mountains: Chapter 1
chapter.title: Paradise

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where are we? Is it all over?

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: That's right, it's all over, and everyone's been restored.

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: What is it? Why are you worrying your lips like that? Are you so moved at seeing me that you have to keep yourselves from crying?

dialogues.speaker: Kshama & Venipi
dialogues.text: AHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHA!

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Ahahaha... K—Kshama, stop... don't laugh... You're going to... give the joke away!

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Laugh all you want. I'm only a little embarrassed.

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Love is fate, as is death — and neither is a laughing matter!

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Fine, fine. No more laughing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, where's Zeitlind, by the way?

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: I've no idea. I was standing outside with everyone else. They were still in each other's arms a moment ago.

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: I told little Scarpa to stop and get everyone back to the main hall. Then I left them and came over to you.

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Everyone should still be somewhere around here. In which case, she can't have gone very far yet.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: This is...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...An amethyst brooch.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: It belongs to my older sister, and was one of the things in my suitcase that I lost.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, got it now! Nice, that's one taken care of.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: It must have been placed here as an exhibit from this era.

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Actually, the reason I started thinking about what to write on my epitaph is because your sister asked about it. Those words weren't exactly things I've been holding in for thousands of years.

dialogues.speaker: Raumhilda
dialogues.text: Does nobody die here? Wouldn't it be impossible for anyone to leave behind a truly magnificent epitaph then?

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Given my former status, I could probably be laid to rest at the priests' cemetery, alongside branches of silver and white.

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Which would be a tremendous honor, albeit one without any space for an epitaph.

dialogues.speaker: Raumhilda
dialogues.text: In that case, it's a no for me. Because I've already written mine.

dialogues.speaker: Raumhilda
dialogues.text: And it says——

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Thank you so much.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And what about that coin of yours? The one from King Deshret's day?

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: You're still thinking about that? Fine, you can have it once I've finished chanting my ten thousand prayers of penance to King Deshret.

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: This one over here got worked up upon hearing Kshama talk about the King's fall that he actually cried, "You lie! You lie!"

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: "You lied! Liar! That's impossible!"

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Honestly, that's better for a laugh than my epitaph.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh, if you're gonna be so grudging with the coin, just forget it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph. And this is the point where we say we're only here to help Zeitlind find what she lost.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're helping you out just 'cause you happened to be here!

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: #...Thank you, Paimon. Thank you, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, no, no. You only got dragged into this because of us. So, we gotta make this right for you.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Such undisguised partiality.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I'm truly grateful to you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you're here, Istoria!

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Indeed. Everyone from the Desert Pavilion is now back at the main hall, which is why I hurried over here.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Zeitlind, have you found what you were looking for?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Yes, I have. Thanks for asking.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Splendid.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: By the way, do you know what the names "Melanta" and "Nihilita" mean?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon will go first! Nope!

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Yes. They mean "melancholy" and "nothingness," don't they?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Most sagacious of you! I believe you and I shall be even better friends than I was with your sister, since we have the same interests.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Yes, my sister's the outdoorsy, extroverted type. Still, before I could read for myself, she used to read to me all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Yet, what has "melancholy" got to do with someone like that?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Of course, I speak of pathological melancholy, not the sort The One above feels when gazing upon on our suffering.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: ...Did she tell you all that?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Frankly, I was agape at the revelations she presented. I wouldn't have thought anyone audacious enough to build a sanatorium atop the site from which the Temple of Space had ascended.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Did you know? It was initially thought that melancholy was a biological ailment. The word itself actually comes from the term for "black bile."

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: But subsequently, people came to believe that melancholy was an affliction of the heart.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, it does take time to get to the right answer...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: But today, humans have once again discovered the truth: melancholy is indeed also pathological. Thus, both medication and companionship are vital to recovery.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: We already knew all that back in my day. The angels had told us so.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: But while the songs of the angels and the latter-day Anemo Archon can cure melancholy, the hollow consolations of ordinary folk cannot be expected to work such wonders.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: What are you trying to say?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I shall to have to whisper this, for it is a secret.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Why would the great One above who rules over sky and space name her own creations "nothingness" and "melancholy"?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: They say she lacks the ability to empathize with others. There is nothing she cannot do, yet she is utterly helpless against genuine futility and the ailments of the human heart.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: This is why she named her creations the two things she is least able to deal with.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon gets that. Naming things after enemies you've never beaten makes them sound cool and powerful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon's would be called "No Mora," "Hunger," and "No {NICKNAME}."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Heh. They sound weak.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I fear I can't keep up with your thousand year's worth of wisdom.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Hahaha! Wisdom? Bah.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I pray for the courage to give this all up and live a real life once more. Can you see what I'm saying?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Feel free to come to me if you ever need anything — even if all you want is to talk about your sister.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I... will do that.

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Don't come any closer!

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: It might be a bit self-indulgent to worry about my own epitaph. You probably think me ridiculous, but I've actually already decided what mine will be.

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: "Please, tell my love in Patraipolis that——"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Vitruvius!

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: ...He turned into sand even before he was done speaking.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm hopeless — I'm actually fighting the urge to chuckle out loud at this sad juncture. He's going to be so mortified once he stops being sand.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: That's a rather optimistic take on the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: We have a choice to make. Do we deal with that guard first? Or search for survivors for as long as we can?

talks.objective: Talk to the person asking for help

dialogues.text: You people... I've not seen you around before. Are there really still newcomers showing up now?

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: But since Dex is with you, I suppose you're backup. My name is Venipi, and I come from an era when King Deshret's divine form still walked among us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon's the name, and this is {NICKNAME}. And our team's got one more member, Zeitlind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're probably what you consider people from the most recent era.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Zeitlind... Would you happen to have an older sister, by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Do you know my sister too?

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Of course. Here, everyone is friends with everyone. It matters little what station they occupied in their former life.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: In my day, I was a nobody, just one of many working on King Deshret's mausoleum.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: I was traveling in the desert one day when I was suddenly plucked from the sands and thrown into the Apathic Interval, where I was for... I want to say less than a hundred years?

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Then, once I left and came here, I found the place full of ancients, some from times preceding even King Deshret himself. But we all got along just the same.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Later on, the sisters of the deity here told me they hadn't plucked any desert buildings, and asked that I reconstruct them from memory.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: It was only with everyone's help that we managed to build this place at all. But now... look at these ruins.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know, speaking of which, Paimon has a question. Those sand statues out there... are those, um... artworks from your era? You know, from back in King Deshret's day?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Perhaps they were created to serve as a reminder of the impermanence of the physical body and life itself...?

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: ...You truly are different from your sister. You must really enjoy reading, like the others.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Those are people — all of them. They were punished by being turned into sand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa!

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Don't worry, they're all still alive. Death does not exist here. They'll be restored once the problem here is resolved.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, wait — didn't you say that whoever saved you would get that coin King Deshret gave you as a reward?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon bets it's worth a lot of Mora!

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Haha, I'm not handing it over! It's my lucky charm! Besides, it's the only thing I have left to remind me of my old life.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pfft. Since it's so important to you... Alright, guess we'll be super nice and not press you for payment.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Ugh, we've been chatting for too long! Looks like it's here!

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: We don't have time to stand around talking. Are you at least at the level of a novice Remurian Centurion?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There we go again! Paimon doesn't even know what kind of standard this is supposed to be...

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Oof, that was quite something. You're easily at the level of a high-ranking Centurion!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Didn't you have your own hierarchy back in King Deshret's day?

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Well, those scholars at the Mahavaipulya Archives have read enough books that their combat assessments actually hold some weight.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Ah, it's nice to be so well read.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: For instance...

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: On average, the knights serving under Erinnyes could take on three standard Remurian Centurions at once, though they're half a rank below Erinnyes.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Medjay, who served the Crocodile King, wasn't considered exactly an elite fighter, but was highly adept at dealing with monsters. So in terms of rough power level...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, let's go save your friends first!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But I wanna know more.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We can talk about that later!

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Venipi! You're still alive! How wonderful to see you!

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Of course I know that death is not possible here. What I mean is, I'm so glad you didn't turn into sand.

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Anyway, you know what I mean.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: I do.

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: And thanks to all of you, and Dex too.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I didn't do a thing.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Venipi introduces you all to Vitruvius and recounts what just happened...

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: Incredible — your strength exceeds even that of a typical Chief Centurion!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now, even Paimon's kinda interested to see how you actually stack up in that system.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oh yeah?

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: In that case, I'll take you to the others.

dialogues.speaker: Vitruvius
dialogues.text: After all, Venipi only provided the pattern work and motifs from King Deshret's times. I was the one responsible for the main layout and pathways in this area.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: That's right. While this may look like a building from some gilded age, it's really the result of everyone's knowledge.

Look for, and rescue, survivor(s) at the Desert Pavilion

dialogues.speaker: Kshama
dialogues.text: Venipi! Dex! And Raumhilda and our new friends! Thank you all!

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: ...I'm her younger sister Zeitlind.

dialogues.speaker: Kshama
dialogues.text: I see. The two of you look so much alike, and oh so pretty. My name is Kshama, and I come from... Ah, what was I going to say?

dialogues.speaker: Kshama
dialogues.text: I see. The two of you look so much alike, and oh so pretty. My name is Kshama, and I come from Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's era.

dialogues.speaker: Kshama
dialogues.text: The era in which the Dendro Archon had yet to become a child.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Venipi introduces Kshama, and Vitruvius's tragic circumstances are revealed...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: They also speak of the epitaph he took thousands of years to come up with.

dialogues.speaker: Kshama
dialogues.text: That is beyond absurd.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: If I hadn't told you, you would never have known.

dialogues.speaker: Kshama
dialogues.text: Now that you have, it's going to be hard for me to look Vitruvius in the eye without laughing.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Alright, enough small talk. We've come all this way, and it doesn't look like we've missed anything.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Is there anyone else?

dialogues.speaker: Kshama
dialogues.text: I'm afraid not.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Then how about how we can stop folks from turning into sand? Any ideas?

dialogues.speaker: Kshama
dialogues.text: We didn't manage to learn much from exploring earlier. After all, no one here at the Desert Pavilion is well-versed in the mystic arts or the sciences.

dialogues.speaker: Kshama
dialogues.text: So, it seems we're back to the only known method: defeating the Punisher of Gomorrah.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: #That you need not worry about. We have {NICKNAME}, who has the strength of a Remurian Tribune.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Looks like someone's been promoted again.

dialogues.speaker: Kshama
dialogues.text: But there's no way to find the Punisher of Gomorrah. It has hidden its form.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: That is a problem, yes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know, it wasn't easy getting everyone out. How about we leave this place first and get back to the main hall?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Istoria and Josephus are there too. They seem rather knowledgeable, so maybe they know a way.

dialogues.speaker: Kshama
dialogues.text: Oh, Istoria's safe too? That's really good to know. He's the most experienced of us all, and is always open to learning new things.

dialogues.speaker: Kshama
dialogues.text: If we're talking about anecdotes, history, and culture, he's probably the most knowledgeable person in this world.

dialogues.speaker: Venipi
dialogues.text: Then let's go now. The earlier we get back, the earlier we can figure this out and save Vitruvius and the rest!

Find a way to leave this place
